5229-felix-o-day.title: Felix O Day
5229-felix-o-day.creator: F. Hopkinson Smith
5229-felix-o-day.description: A book by F. Hopkinson Smith. me flaunt signs of “Standing Room Only.” The cars still follow their routes, lunging and pausing like huge beetles; but much of the wheel traffic has melted, with only here and there a cab or truck between which gold-splashed umbrellas pick a hazardous way.

arxiv-2109-15165.title: Euclidean numbers and numerosities
arxiv-2109-15165.creator: Vieri Benci, Lorenzo Luperi Baglini
arxiv-2109-15165.description: Abstract Several different versions of the theory of numerosities have been introduced in the literature. Here, we unify these approaches in a consistent frame through the notion of set of labels, relating numerosities with the Kiesler field of Euclidean numbers.

arxiv-2206-01964.title: Indecomposable characters on direct limit of symmetric groups with diagonal embeddings
arxiv-2206-01964.creator: N. Nessonov, N. T. S. Ngo
arxiv-2206-01964.description: Abstract In this paper we obtain the complete description of all indecomposable characters (central positive-definite functions) of inductive limits of the symmetric groups under block diagonal embedding. As a corollary we obtain the full classification of the isomorphism classes of these inductive limits. Keywords: Infinite symmetric group; Character; Factor representation.

arxiv-2212-09619.title: A spinorial quasilocal mass
arxiv-2212-09619.creator: John Lott Department of Mathematics University of California, Berkeley Berkeley, CA 94720-3840 USA
arxiv-2212-09619.description: Abstract . We define a quasilocal energy of a compact manifold-with-boundary, relative to a background manifold. The construction uses spinors on one manifold and the pullback of dual spinors from the other manifold. We prove positivity results for the quasilocal energy, in both the Riemannian and Lorentzian settings. 1 1 1 lott@berkeley.edu 1.

arxiv-2307-15239.title: Distinctive pupil and microsaccade-rate signatures in self-recognition
arxiv-2307-15239.creator: Lisa Schwetlick 1,3,6,∗, Hendrik Graupner 2,4, Olaf Dimigen 5, Ralf Engbert 1,3
arxiv-2307-15239.description: Abstract Pupil dynamics and fixational eye movements are primarily involuntary processes that actively support visual perception during fixations. Both measures are known to be sensitive to ongoing cognitive and affective processing. In a visual fixation experiment ( N N =116) we demonstrate that self-recognition, familiar faces, and unfamiliar faces elicit specific responses in pupil dynamics and microsaccade rate.

arxiv-2408-11815.title: Great Memory, Shallow Reasoning: Limits of k k NN-LMs
arxiv-2408-11815.creator: Shangyi Geng, Wenting Zhao, Alexander M Rush
arxiv-2408-11815.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shangyi Geng, Wenting Zhao, Alexander M Rush. K K -nearest neighbor language models ( k k NN-LMs), which integrate retrieval with next-word prediction, have demonstrated strong performance in language modeling as well as downstream NLP benchmarks. These results have led researchers to argue that models trained on poor quality or outdated data could perform well by employing a k k NN extension that has access to a higher-quality datastore.

arxiv-2505-05982.title: On the Potential of Electrified Supply Chains to Provide Long Duration Demand Flexibility
arxiv-2505-05982.creator: Rina Davila Severiano, Constance Crozier, and Mark O’Mailley
arxiv-2505-05982.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rina Davila Severiano, Constance Crozier, and Mark O’Mailley. Demand flexibility can offset some of the variability introduced on the supply-side by variable renewable generation. However, most efforts (e.g. control of residential vehicle charging) focus on short durations – typically on the scale of minutes to hours. This paper investigates whether a fully electrified supply chain (transport and manufacturing) could provide demand flexibility over longer durations, exploiting the latency that typically exists between the processing of raw material to the delivery of finished product.

arxiv-2510-08613.title: GraphGhost: Tracing Structures Behind Large Language Models
arxiv-2510-08613.creator: Xinnan Dai, Kai Guo, Chung-Hsiang Lo, Shenglai Zeng, Jiayuan Ding, Dongsheng Luo, Subhabrata Mukherjee, Jiliang Tang
arxiv-2510-08613.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable reasoning capabilities, yet the structural mechanisms underlying these abilities remain under explored. In this work, we introduce GraphGhost, a unified framework that represents neuron activations and their signal propagation as graphs, explaining how LLMs capture structural semantics from sequential inputs and generate outputs through structurally consistent mechanisms.

arxiv-2510-13154.title: I Am Aligned, But With Whom? MENA Values Benchmark for Evaluating Cultural Alignment and Multilingual Bias in LLMs
arxiv-2510-13154.creator: Pardis Sadat Zahraei, Ehsaneddin Asgari
arxiv-2510-13154.description: Abstract We introduce MENAValues, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the cultural alignment and multilingual biases of large language models (LLMs) with respect to the beliefs and values of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, an underrepresented area in current AI evaluation efforts.

arxiv-2510-14645.title: Block-Partitioning Strategies for Accelerated Multi-rate Encoding in Adaptive VVC Streaming
arxiv-2510-14645.creator: Vignesh V Menon 1 , Adam Wieckowski 1 , Yiquin Liu 1 , Benjamin Bross 1 , Detlev Marpe 1
arxiv-2510-14645.description: Abstract The demand for efficient multi-rate encoding techniques has surged with the increasing prevalence of ultra-high-definition (UHD) video content, particularly in adaptive streaming scenarios where a single video must be encoded at multiple bitrates to accommodate diverse network conditions. While Versatile Video Coding (VVC) significantly improves compression efficiency, it introduces considerable computational complexity, making multi-rate encoding a resource-intensive task.

arxiv-2511-19306.title: Dual-Granularity Semantic Prompting for Language Guidance Infrared Small Target Detection
arxiv-2511-19306.creator: Zixuan Wang, Haoran Sun, Jiaming Lu, Wenxuan Wang, Zhongling Huang, Dingwen Zhang, Xuelin Qian, Junwei Han, School of Automation, Northwestern Polytechnical University
arxiv-2511-19306.description: Abstract Infrared small target detection remains challenging due to limited feature representation and severe background interference, resulting in sub-optimal performance. While recent CLIP-inspired methods attempt to leverage textual guidance for detection, they are hindered by inaccurate text descriptions and reliance on manual annotations. To overcome these limitations, we propose DGSPNet, an end-to-end language prompt-driven framework.

arxiv-2512-20675.title: Revisiting the learning objectives of vision-language reward models
arxiv-2512-20675.creator: Simon Roy, Samuel Barbeau, Giovanni Beltrame, Christian Desrosiers, Nicolas Thome
arxiv-2512-20675.description: Abstract Learning generalizable reward functions is a core challenge in embodied intelligence. Recent work leverages contrastive vision language models (VLMs) to obtain dense, domain-agnostic rewards without human supervision. These methods adapt VLMs into reward models through increasingly complex learning objectives, yet meaningful comparison remains difficult due to differences in training data, architectures, and evaluation settings.

arxiv-2512-24590.title: Two-Distance Sets over Finite Fields
arxiv-2512-24590.creator: Jozsef Solymosi
arxiv-2512-24590.description: Abstract We show that Blokhuis’ quadratic upper bound for two-distance sets is sharp over finite fields in almost all dimensions. Our construction complements Lisoněk’s higher-dimensional maximal constructions that carried out in Lorentz spaces [ 6 ] . 1 Introduction The study of few-distance sets is a classical topic at the interface of discrete geometry, algebraic combinatorics, and harmonic analysis.

britannica-1911-white-gilbert.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica

pmc-10561648.title: Experimental and Theoretical Evaluation of the Thermodynamics of the Carbonation Reaction of ZIF-8 and Its Close-Packed Polymorph with Carbon Dioxide
pmc-10561648.creator: Gerson
pmc-10561648.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). We report the first experimental and theoretical evaluation of the thermodynamic driving force for the reaction of metal–organic framework (MOF) materials with carbon dioxide, leading to a metal–organic carbonate phase. Carbonation upon exposure of MOFs to CO2 is a significant concern for the design and deployment of such materials in carbon storage technologies, and this work shows that the formation of a carbonate material from the popular SOD-topology framework material ZIF-8, as well as its dense-packed dia-topology polymorph, is significantly exothermic.

pmc-10709103.title: The Effect of Passion for Outdoor Activities on Employee Well-Being Using Nature Connectedness as the Mediating Variable and Environmental Identity as the Moderating Variable
pmc-10709103.creator: Chunyu Zhang, Xiao Ma, Liping Liu
pmc-10709103.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). PurposeAlthough prior research has found outdoor activities to be an important effect on employee well-being, the mechanisms of their effect are understudied. This study integrated the Broaden-and-Build Theory, Attention Restoration Theory and Cognitive Assessment Theory to examine the relation between passion for outdoor activities (two dimensions, namely, harmonious passion, obsessive passion) and employee well-being (three dimensions, namely, life well-being, workplace well-being, psychological well-being) by the mediating role of nature connectedness and the moderating role of environmental identity.Participants and MethodsData were collected from

pmc-11289365.title: Machine learning-guided co-optimization of fitness and diversity facilitates combinatorial library design in enzyme engineering
pmc-11289365.creator: Kerr Ding, Michael Chin, Yunlong Zhao, Wei Huang, Binh Khanh Mai, Huanan Wang, Peng Liu, Yang Yang, Yunan Luo
pmc-11289365.description: The effective design of combinatorial libraries to balance fitness and diversity facilitates the engineering of useful enzyme functions, particularly those that are poorly characterized or unknown in biology. We introduce MODIFY, a machine learning (ML) algorithm that learns from natural protein sequences to infer evolutionarily plausible mutations and predict enzyme fitness.

pmc-11470608.title: Ankle syndesmotic ligaments avulsion fractures: incidence in adult population
pmc-11470608.creator: Xiang Yao, Chong Wang, Weijie Pan, Yicong Chao, Jilei Tang
pmc-11470608.description: BackgroundDistal tibiofibular syndesmosis injury is often associated with ankle fractures in adults. Injuries to the anterior/posterior inferior tibiofibular ligament (AITFL/PITFL) may present as a mid-substance tear or as an avulsion at insertion. Tibial and fibular avulsion of the AITFL is known as Tillaux fracture and Wagstaffe fracture, respectively.

pmc-11595130.title: Functional Mitral Regurgitation Post-Isolated Aortic Valve Replacement
pmc-11595130.creator: Petar Dabic, Bojan Vucurevic, Milorad Sevkovic, Dusan Andric, Slobodan Pesic, Mihailo Neskovic, Sasa Borovic, Jovan Petrovic, Anna Kabłak-Ziembicka
pmc-11595130.description: Background: The management of mitral regurgitation during aortic valve replacement remains a complex question. Secondary mitral regurgitation often improves post-aortic valve replacement without mitral valve surgery, but residual mitral regurgitation can significantly affect long-term outcomes. This study investigates the natural history of mitral regurgitation following isolated aortic valve replacement and identifies prognostic factors for persistent mitral regurgitation.

pmc-12472506.title: Transplacental Transmission of Cytomegalovirus (CMV) in Pregnant Women with Positive Anti-CMV IgG and Negative Anti-CMV IgM in Highly CMV Seropositive Region
pmc-12472506.creator: Jie Tang, Hongxia Wei, Yimin Dai, Yuqian Luo, Yali Hu, Yi-Hua Zhou, Nacheng Lin, Aimin Liu
pmc-12472506.description: Primary or recurrent infection of cytomegalovirus (CMV) in pregnant women may cause transplacental transmission to fetuses. We aimed to investigate the rate of transplacental CMV transmission in women with positive anti-CMV IgG and negative anti-CMV IgM and its impact on newborns.

pmc-12731487.title: Validation of the Greek Version of the Colorado Learning Difficulties Questionnaire
pmc-12731487.creator: Eleni Panagiota Fefe, Xanthi Tigani, Maria Michou, Vasiliki Efthymiou, Antonios I Christou, Christina Darviri, Maria Charalampopoulou, Emmanouil Apostolakis, Stavroula Papadodima, Christina Kanaka-Gantenbein, Flora Bacopoulou, Cristina Nunes
pmc-12731487.description: Highlights What are the main findings? The Greek validation of the Colorado Learning Difficulties Questionnaire (CLDQ) demonstrated satisfactory reliability and strong construct validity among Greek parents and caregivers.Exploratory factor analyses supported a five-factor structure (Reading, Mathematics, Social Cognition, Social Anxiety, and Spatial Problems) consistent with the original version, with minor item variations. What is the implication of the main finding?

pmc-13292183.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models for Cancer Immunotherapy
pmc-13292183.creator: Xinchao Wu, Mengtao Sun, Lusheng Li, Jieqiong Wang, Shibiao Wan
pmc-13292183.description: Cancer immunotherapy, which leverages the immune system to combat tumor cells, has made significant advancements in oncology treatment in recent years. Yet significant challenges remain in predicting treatment responses and understanding mechanisms of resistance. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) provide powerful tools to address these challenges, enabling breakthroughs in patient stratification, biomarker discovery, and treatment strategy optimization.

pmc-13445862.title: Dialogues of delivery: a multilingual question-answer dataset for maternal healthcare in East African languages
pmc-13445862.creator: Richard Kimera, Rogers Kuyeso, Emmanuel Maleka, Fortunate Tukamushaba, Wasswa William, Rogers Mwavu, David Sabiiti Bamutura, Joseph Ngonzi, Brenda Ainomugisha, Alexer Namuli, Proscovia Namiiro, Clare Nyakato, Leo Anthony Celi, Fred Kaggwa
pmc-13445862.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThere is a critical scarcity of domain-specific, clinically grounded Natural Language Processing (NLP) resources for African languages. In Western Uganda, linguistic diversity creates a barrier to maternal healthcare, as mothers lack access to health information in their native languages.

pmc-13482614.title: Direct correspondence between liquid and glass polymorphism in densely packed metallic alloys
pmc-13482614.creator: Hongbo Lou, Xiaoxing Ke, Xin Zhang, Lianghua Xiong, Fujun Lan, Aiguo Li, Zhidan Zeng, Hongwei Sheng, Ho-kwang Mao, Qiaoshi Zeng
pmc-13482614.description: Liquid and glass are two closely related disordered states of matter. Whether each can exhibit two or more structurally distinct yet chemically identical forms have been debated for decades and the relationship between polymorphism in equilibrium liquids and that in non-equilibrium glasses remains elusive.
